item.title: Man who beat rare cancer celebrates by canoeing 2,000 miles with his dog
item.description: Frank Carter, 67, and his dog Amos completed a 2,000-mile canoe trip down the Missouri River four years after CAR T-cell therapy cleared his lymphoma.
item.content:encoded:
A 67-year-old cancer survivor from Orange County, Florida, completed a more than 2,000-mile journey down the Missouri River alongside his dog, Amos, after undergoing a groundbreaking immunotherapy treatment.

Frank Carter spent 64 days navigating the longest U.S. river in a cedar-strip canoe he built by hand, according to reports from the Moffitt Cancer Center and FOX 13 News.

The expedition began in Montana and concluded near St. Louis, Missouri, requiring the pair to camp along the riverbank while enduring severe storms, high winds and hail, FOX 13 News reported.

'FIT MOM' DID 'EVERYTHING RIGHT' — THEN A COLON CANCER DIAGNOSIS CHANGED HER LIFE

Before his diagnosis, Carter was a long-distance adventurer. According to the Moffitt Cancer Center, he spent five months hiking the Appalachian Trail in 2019 and completed an eight-week cross-country bicycle ride from San Diego to New Smyrna Beach, Florida, in 2020.

However, his physical limits were tested in a new way in 2021 following a routine 5K race.

"I was wiped out. I just wasn't recovering," Carter told FOX 13 News. "I went to my doctor, had blood tests. Long story short, in two weeks I was getting chemo."

Doctors diagnosed Carter with mantle cell lymphoma, a rare form of blood cancer that originates in white blood cells known as lymphocytes. He underwent 15 rounds of chemotherapy in Orlando, according to Moffitt Cancer Center.

Although the treatment significantly reduced the cancer, follow-up exams showed lingering traces of the disease.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Carter then sought care at the Moffitt Cancer Center in Tampa to undergo chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, which involves extracting the patient's own immune cells, genetically altering them in a laboratory to identify cancer cells, and adding them back into the body.

"We take those T-cells and genetically engineer them by putting something called a CAR into them," Dr. Michael Jain, an oncologist at Moffitt Cancer Center, told FOX 13 News. "Now these T-cells can see the tumor and get rid of it, where before the tumor was able to hide from it."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Carter has remained cancer-free for four years following the single infusion. Throughout his recovery, he has found constant support in his dog, Amos, whom he brought home right before beginning chemotherapy.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

"After my cancer diagnosis, I told myself I was going to beat this, and I really wanted a dog during the process," Carter told Moffitt's Endeavor publication. "I got Amos right before my first treatment."

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Alleged $32M COVID-19 fraud fugitive captured in Jamaica and returned to US, FBI says
item.description: Elaine Angene Escoe was living under the fake identity "Harley Newman" in Jamaica before her arrest in connection with a $32 million COVID-19 fraud scheme.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: One of the FBI's most wanted alleged COVID-19 fraud fugitives has been returned to the United States after authorities captured her in Jamaica, where FBI Director Kash Patel told Fox News Digital she had been living under the fake identity "Harley Newman" while evading charges tied to a $32 million pandemic relief fraud scheme.

Elaine Angene Escoe, 41, arrived back in South Florida Thursday after Jamaican authorities arrested her following a federal manhunt. Prosecutors allege she helped fraudulently obtain more than $32 million in taxpayer-funded COVID-19 relief funds before fleeing the country after failing to appear in federal court.

Escoe was indicted in 2025 on charges including conspiracy to commit wire fraud, wire fraud, conspiracy to commit money laundering and multiple counts of money laundering, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern District of Florida.

EXCLUSIVE: FBI ADDS ALLEGED COVID FRAUDSTER ACCUSED OF TAKING $5M FROM KIDS' MEAL PROGRAM TO MOST WANTED LIST

Federal prosecutors said a judge issued an arrest warrant after Escoe failed to appear in court in May 2025. Authorities allege she fled to Jamaica, where she was later located and arrested after the FBI received a tip.

"Elaine Angene Escoe's arrest and return to the United States demonstrates that no one is beyond the reach of American justice," Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche said.

Blanche said Escoe is accused of participating in a multimillion-dollar scheme to defraud taxpayer-funded COVID-19 relief programs and said the Justice Department will continue prosecuting those who steal from the American people.

FBI NABS ALLEGED $547M MEDICARE FRAUD FUGITIVE OVERSEAS, THIRD CAPTURE FROM 'MOST WANTED FRAUDSTERS' LIST

Patel called Escoe's arrest another milestone in the FBI's international fraud crackdown, saying she is the fourth alleged "Most Wanted Fraudster" captured in the past five weeks.

"The historic success of the 'Most Wanted Fraudster' list continues as the FBI and our partners just captured our fourth Most Wanted Fraudster in 5 weeks, and yet another high value target returned to the U.S. by this FBI," Patel said. "Elaine Angene Escoe, on the run since May 2025, was captured in Jamaica while living under a fake identity of 'Harley Newman' — and returned to the United States today to face justice."

Patel said Escoe is charged with being involved in a conspiracy to commit wire fraud and money laundering connected to a scheme that fraudulently obtained more than $32 million in federal COVID-19 relief funds.

He added that the FBI has returned more than 30 high-value targets to the U.S. since June. Patel said four alleged fraud suspects captured over the past five weeks are collectively charged with nearly $1.8 billion in fraud after spending more than 3,500 days on the run across three continents.

"Under this administration, fraud is no longer tolerated — and those who steal from American taxpayers have nowhere to hide," Patel said.

Authorities said the FBI, Homeland Security Investigations, the U.S. Marshals Service, Jamaican law enforcement and the Palm Beach County State Attorney's Office coordinated Escoe's return to the U.S.

item.title: Brooke Burke flaunts toned figure in green bikini during barefoot Malibu beach stroll
item.description: Brooke Burke stuns in a green bikini on a Malibu beach walk, weeks after sharing family vacation photos from Cabo San Lucas with fiancé Scott Rigsby.
item.content:encoded:
Brooke Burke is flaunting her toned body while taking a stroll on the beach in Malibu.

The 54-year-old TV personality and model was recently photographed walking barefoot along the shoreline in Malibu in a green bikini, which she paired with a necklace, gold earrings and a stack of bracelets.

The bikini top featured a crisscrossed pattern which gave a peek at her chest, and her bottoms had a matching pattern.

This is far from the first time Burke has been photographed posing in her bikini on the beach. Just last month, the "Penn & Teller: Fool Us" host was all smiles as she walked along the water in Malibu in an orange and blue patterned bikini with cutouts.

BELLA HADID, KELSEA BALLERINI AND OTHER STARS KICK OFF SUMMER EARLY WITH BIKINI PHOTOS

When it comes to keeping her toned figure, Burke broke down her three-hour health and beauty routine to Fox News Digital in May 2025, admitting it sounds weird.

"This castor oil belly button detox that's popping right now on social media, I got suckered. I ordered a kit," Burke began.

She then explained that she will apply castor oil to her stomach and wrap herself in a big bandage, which she then sleeps with, noting, "I think personally, because it looks so weird, that's why everyone's interested."

After removing the bandage in the morning, Burke said she will typically perform a lymphatic drainage massage on herself and rubs in the remaining oil.

"It actually works for bloating, detoxing. Skin quality is great. And I think it might be… maybe part of it's mental – you know, I'm always a skeptic and I keep it real – but it might also be the intention of kind of loving your belly a little bit and doing a belly massage and just taking care of yourself," she said. "So yeah, weird, I know, I like weird things."

GISELE BÜNDCHEN CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY IN LEOPARD-PRINT BIKINI AS SHE REFLECTS ON GRATITUDE

Burke recently shared her own bikini photos from a recent family vacation to Cabo San Lucas, Mexico, captioning the post, "My kind of roll @nobuloscabos you were everything."

The photos showed Burke enjoying the pool with her children, some of her cuddling with her fiancé, Scott Rigsby, as well as a few of her doing yoga and exercising while on vacation.

"Love this family so much! Gorgeous inside and out," one fan wrote in the comments section. Another added, "Gorgeous pics Brooke."

Burke and Rigsby made their relationship public in August 2019, and announced their engagement in September 2021, shortly after her 50th birthday.

The couple discussed their long engagement during an interview with People in June 2024, with Burke telling the outlet, "I'm not rushing."

"I think for us, it's having the experience," Rigsby said. "I mean, the whole reason to do it, too, is for the kids and for us and the family. So we want to do it right. We just don't want to rush into it."

item.title: Longer lives, worse health? Scientists uncover troubling trend across generations
item.description: The morbidity gap between life expectancy and healthy life expectancy is widest in America, where people spend about 14 years in poor health.
item.content:encoded:
People across the world are living longer, but they’re also spending more years coping with ill health, a recent study observed.

The "morbidity gap" — the number of years people spend in poor health, typically struggling with chronic challenges such as low back pain, hearing loss and depression — widened across 203 of 204 countries analyzed, and was the most pronounced in America, the researchers found.

"Globally in 2023, an average of 14·5% of life was spent in poor health, compared to 13·6% in 1990," the researchers at the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation at the University of Washington reported.

JANE SEYMOUR, 75, SHARES HOW SHE APPROACHES AGING WITH VITALITY: 'BEST I CAN BE'

In the United States, the morbidity gap is about 14 years, or 17.8% of the expected lifespan.

"Between 1990 and 2023, global life expectancy at birth increased from 64.6 years to 73.8 years, while healthy life expectancy rose from 55.9 years to 63.1 years," the researchers reported in a news release.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

"Because gains in survival consistently outpaced gains in healthy years of life, people are spending more years living with chronic disease and disability," they wrote.

The gap widened the most in the wealthiest countries where populations have access to life-extending resources, the researchers reported. Women are also living longer than men, but also spending more years in poor health, they found.

"To me, the most important message of this study is not that people are living longer — it is that we have become far better at delaying death than delaying functional decline," Dr. Antony Chu, clinical assistant professor at Brown University’s Warren Alpert School of Medicine, told Fox News Digital.

"Modern medicine has achieved remarkable success in reducing mortality from cardiovascular disease, cancer, trauma and infectious illness," he said. "Yet many of those additional years are now lived with chronic pain, disability, sensory loss, depression or reduced independence."

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Researchers analyzed Global Burden of Disease data covering 204 countries and territories from 1990 through 2023. In their report, published by The Lancet Public Health, scientists observed that a small number of chronic, largely non-fatal causes were the primary contributors to the morbidity gap.

Musculoskeletal disorders, especially low back pain, mental disorders, such as depression and anxiety, hearing loss, falls and other non-communicable accounted for about 57% of all years lived in poor health worldwide. High fasting plasma glucose, obesity and aging populations were also important contributors.

The researchers noted that the study points to broad health trends but doesn’t prove exactly what's causing people to spend more years in poor health.

"Our findings suggest that future gains in population health will come not only from helping people live longer, but from helping them live healthier," said Dr. Christopher Murray, director of the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) at the University of Washington School of Medicine and senior author of the study.

"Progress in healthy aging should be measured not only by lifespan, but by healthspan [the number of years spent in good health], with greater investment in prevention, long-term disease management and chronic care to reduce years lived in poor health," Murray added.

The goal should no longer be simply extending lifespan, but compressing morbidity and maximizing the number of years people remain physically, cognitively and socially well, Chu told Fox News Digital.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

"Ultimately, I believe the next frontier of medicine is not simply adding years to life, but adding life to years," he said. "First, we need to focus on preserving function rather than simply reacting to disease."

The approach involves routinely assessing mobility, muscle strength, balance, hearing, cognition and overall physical resilience. Chu said this may prove just as important as monitoring blood pressure, cholesterol and glucose.

"Functional decline often begins years before disability becomes obvious, providing an opportunity for earlier intervention," he said.

Musculoskeletal health also deserves much greater emphasis, Chu said.

"Progressive resistance training, fall prevention, maintenance of muscle mass and early treatment of chronic back pain should become core components of preventive medicine rather than afterthoughts," he said. "Preserving mobility may ultimately have as much impact on healthy aging as preventing heart disease."

Mental health and social connection are another vital component to healthspan, Chu said.

"Hearing loss, depression, anxiety and loneliness frequently reinforce one another, accelerating physical decline while diminishing quality of life," he said. "Addressing these conditions early may improve both longevity and independence."

Chu, who is the child of immigrants, said it’s his belief that Americans often overlook an important cultural dimension of healthy aging.

"In many societies outside the United States, older adults continue to play an active and respected role within multigenerational families," he said. "They remain mentors, caregivers, historians and sources of wisdom. This continued sense of purpose and belonging may provide meaningful protection against loneliness, depression and loss of identity."

"By contrast, many older Americans experience increasing social isolation precisely when maintaining meaningful relationships may be most important," Chu added. "Healthy aging is not determined solely by biology; it is also shaped by community, purpose and human connection."

item.title: Rep Brandon Gill backs Trump executive order, calls to 'clean house' at the Smithsonian
item.description: Rep. Brandon Gill says Americans are "sick" of woke ideology at taxpayer-funded museums and praises Trump for confronting ideological bias head-on.
item.content:encoded:
Rep. Brandon Gill, R-Texas, threw his support behind President Donald Trump's executive action targeting alleged ideological bias at the Smithsonian and called for museum officials to be fired over what he called left-wing influence at the institution.

Speaking on "Fox & Friends Weekend," Gill applauded Trump's directive to place warning signs along National Park Service walkways outside the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History.

"This is the first time, I think, that we've had a president who takes this stuff seriously, who doesn't just look the other way and allow the left to continue their long march through the institutions and continue shoving leftism down our throats and down the throats of our children," Gill said. "I think that's what is so refreshing about the president here."

TRUMP ORDERS SIGNS OUTSIDE SMITHSONIAN MUSEUM AMID ROW OVER ITS DEPICTION OF AMERICAN HISTORY

On Friday, Trump signed an executive order directing officials to install signs outside the Smithsonian's National Museum of American History informing visitors about the White House report that criticized the museum's portrayal of American history.

"Such signage shall notify visitors that the Museum exhibits should be renovated consistent with the findings in the Report and direct visitors to locations and resources for accurate information regarding America's history," according to the executive order on the White House website.

The order also calls for the creation of temporary exhibits or signage that "corrects inaccurate information presented in the Museum," pointing to the museum's alleged failure to properly commemorate America's founding history during its 250th anniversary year.

REP GILL CHALLENGES 'GENUINELY INSANE AND OBJECTIVELY OFFENSIVE' DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS AFTER VIRAL HEARING

Gill echoed many of the administration's critiques, calling for what he described as an objective telling of American history.

"We need an actual objective telling of American history, not [looking] back on the American story and grouping different people into racial or ethnic groups or groups based on their gender or their sexuality or their immigration status," he said. "We are one American people, and I think that's what we need to see."

The congressman argued the Smithsonian needed to "clean house," specifically calling for National Museum of American History Director Anthea Hartig to be fired. Gill added that the American public is exhausted by watching taxpayer dollars fund ideological agendas.

THE WOKE LEFT CAPTURED THE SMITHSONIAN. AMERICA NEEDS A PATRIOT TO TAKE IT BACK

"The American people are so sick of seeing the left take control of iconic American institutions," he said. "They want to see a museum that's funded by taxpayers that is promoting patriotism, that promotes American ideals and values, and instead they get this kind of woke nonsense."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Smithsonian for comment but did not immediately hear back.

The controversy stems from the White House's recent "Saving America's Story" report. In the executive order, Trump said the report demonstrated that the museum's leadership "does not present American history as a shared national inheritance to be taught and celebrated, but instead views American history as a 'prime tool' to advance ideas of social justice and the radical transformation of our society."

Hartig defended the museum's approach during a committee hearing earlier this week.

"The museum does not take sides in America’s political debates. We preserve and document the evidence of American life in all its breadth so that the public can encounter the past and draw their own conclusions," Hartig said.

"When historians talk about reframing a traditional narrative, we do not mean erasing it. We mean adding the evidence, voices and objects that earlier tellings left out so that more Americans can see themselves in the national story. Examining the harder chapters of our history is not the same as hostility toward America," she said.

item.title: Court checks Pritzker as Trump administration scores another immigration win
item.description: A federal judge ruled Illinois laws providing in-state tuition and financial aid to illegal immigrants are unconstitutional, dealing a blow to JB Pritzker.
item.content:encoded:
Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker was dealt a major legal blow Friday after a federal judge gutted key state laws providing in-state tuition, financial aid and scholarships to illegal immigrants, marking another win for the Trump administration's nationwide immigration agenda.

U.S. District Judge Stephen McGlynn, a Trump appointee serving in the Southern District of Illinois, sided with the Justice Department, ruling that Illinois' in-state tuition policies, the RISE Act and the Illinois DREAM Act are "unconstitutional and invalid" as applied to illegal immigrants.

The ruling permanently prevents Illinois from enforcing the laws, although McGlynn delayed the order from taking effect for 14 days to allow the state to ask an appeals court to intervene.

JUSTICE DEPARTMENT SUES COLORADO OVER IN-STATE TUITION AND FINANCIAL AID FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS

U.S. Attorney Steven Weinhoeft celebrated the ruling.

"Illinois sought to incentivize illegal immigration on the taxpayer's dime by treating illegal aliens better than U.S. citizens living in other states, in clear violation of federal law," Weinhoeft said in a statement. "This ruling enforces the statute Congress wrote and stops the State from putting illegal aliens ahead of American citizens."

The decision is the latest victory for the Trump administration's effort to dismantle state laws extending higher education benefits to illegal immigrants and comes one day after the Justice Department filed a similar lawsuit against Colorado.

NEBRASKA ENDS IN-STATE TUITION BENEFITS FOR ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS UNDER DOJ DEAL

The Justice Department filed the lawsuit against Illinois and a handful of colleges in September 2025, arguing that Illinois violated federal law by offering in-state tuition and financial aid to illegal immigrants without making those same benefits available to all U.S. citizens regardless of where they live.

McGlynn granted the federal government's motion for summary judgment and denied Illinois' motion to dismiss.

The ruling invalidates Illinois' in-state tuition rules, the RISE Act, which provides access to state financial aid for certain students ineligible for federal aid, and the Illinois DREAM Act, which established scholarship opportunities for eligible students.

DOJ ESCALATES BLUE-STATE ICE STANDOFF AFTER STATES REFUSE KEY FEDERAL REQUEST

Rep. Mary Miller, R-Ill. praised the decision on X.

"This is a win for Illinois taxpayers and American students who were shut out while Pritzker prioritized foreigners in our country illegally," Miller wrote.

The Justice Department has won or reached settlements in similar cases involving Texas, Kentucky, Oklahoma and Nebraska, with Nebraska agreeing to end in-state tuition benefits for illegal immigrants as part of a settlement. Lawsuits remain pending against Minnesota, Virginia, California, New Jersey, Kansas, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Maryland and now Colorado.

In its lawsuit filed Thursday against Colorado, the Justice Department argued the state's ASSET Act and related policies unlawfully provide lower tuition rates and state financial aid to illegal immigrants while denying those same benefits to out-of-state U.S. citizens.

"For three decades, Congress has made clear that Colorado cannot give education benefits to illegal aliens that it does not give to all American citizens," Associate Attorney General Stanley Woodward said. "By granting illegal aliens in-state tuition, Colorado is not only violating federal law but subsidizing education for illegal aliens at taxpayers' expense."

"Our litigation efforts will not cease until we have fulfilled President Trump's promise that illegal aliens will not obtain preferential treatment over our nation's own citizens," he added.

Colorado Gov. Jared Polis' office defended the state's policies.

"The federal government seizing control of determining in-state tuition across the country is absurd," a Polis spokesperson previously told Fox News Digital. "In Colorado, we are expanding access to education to provide students with the skills to get good-paying jobs and doubling down on strategies to save students money."

Fox News Digital reached out to Pritzker's office for comment.

item.title: NYC 5-alarm fire injures at least 17 firefighters, others as blaze damages multiple apartment buildings
item.description: 5-alarm fire damages multiple buildings in Queens, injuring 17 firefighters and displacing families as 250 FDNY personnel battled the blaze.
item.content:encoded:
Nearly two dozen people were injured, including several New York City firefighters (FDNY) Saturday, when a massive fire broke out at an apartment building in Queens.

FDNY chief of Fire Operations Kevin Woods said firefighters first got word of the fire just before 10 a.m. in a two-story wooden building in Queens and when they arrived, two buildings were fully involved, and it was spreading to a third building.

Woods added that rescuers were able to get to the second floor above the fire "under high heat and zero visibility" where one resident was trapped.

HISTORIC NYC CHURCH ENGULFED IN 5-ALARM BLAZE; 6 FIREFIGHTERS INJURED BATTLING STUBBORN FLAMES

They were taken to the hospital.

In total, 17 firefighters were injured, two members of Emergency Medical Services (EMS) and two civilians.

None of the injuries are life-threatening, Woods said.

PAROLED FELON CHARGED IN DEADLY FIRE AT NEW YORK HOMELESS HOTEL THAT KILLED 6

"We want to thank the staff at all of these area hospitals for taking care of our personnel," Woods added.

He said the fifth-alarm fire, which corresponds to using 250 firefighters, left "heavy damage" to the building and many of the families are displaced.

Woods added that the historic residences were built in 1930 and completely made of wood.

The fire is under control, he said, adding that the cause is under investigation.

item.title: 'Weird Al' Yankovic says he walked away from a seven-figure comedy festival offer in Saudi Arabia
item.description: "Weird Al" Yankovic says he was offered seven figures for one show at the Riyadh Comedy Festival but turned it down because it made him "feel icky."
item.content:encoded:
Musician and comedy icon "Weird Al" Yankovic reportedly turned down an eye-watering "seven figures" to perform at Saudi Arabia’s controversial debut festival last year.

In an interview with Pennsylvania’s Tribune-Review, the Grammy-winning parody artist revealed that he declined an invitation to perform at the inaugural Riyadh Comedy Festival last year, and that the idea of accepting Saudi money as payment made him "feel icky."

"I was invited to the Riyadh Comedy Festival, which is something that I obviously did not want to do," Yankovic reportedly said. "They offered me, I’m not going to say how much, but it was seven figures to do one show, which is way more than I’ve ever been offered in my life to do a show."

DAVE CHAPPELLE SAYS HE’S CONSIDERING REVISITING ‘CHAPPELLE’S SHOW’ DECADES AFTER WALKING AWAY

Yankovic went on to assert that he does not look down on any performers who chose to appear at the controversial festival, which hosted approximately 6,000 attendees, but insisted that he could not stomach the implications of appearing at the event.

"But I just couldn’t be part of that," he continued. "I’m not dissing anybody that took the money because I’m sure everybody that went there got a lot of money. I’m sure they had their own reasons and justifications for doing it. But I’m doing enough that I don’t need to take any amount of money if it makes me feel icky, and that kind of did."

The comedian previously made headlines after he declined to appear in an unspecified AI advertisement, saying he turned down yet another large sum by rejecting the offer.

WHITNEY CUMMINGS CLAIMS LURID TRUMP JOKE WAS CUT FROM NETFLIX'S MARK TWAIN PRIZE SPECIAL

"I wish people would offer me things that I didn’t feel bad about accepting," Yankovic told the Tribune-Review, referring to the AI ad.

Fox News Digital extensively covered the reaction in the comedy world to last year’s Riyadh Comedy Festival, in which key names within the industry offered harsh criticism toward comedians who chose to appear at the event.

At the time, "Real Time" host Bill Maher blasted comedian Dave Chappelle for his choice to perform at the festival.

BILL MAHER TELLS NPR INTERVIEWER HE VIEWS OUTLET AS 'FAR EXTREME OF THE LEFT'

"Dave Chappelle … was in the press today saying that you can speak more freely over here than in America," Maher told Louis C.K., who also made an appearance at the controversial event.

"I don't know if that's true," C.K. replied.

"Oh, it's not true," Maher said, before suggesting that Chappelle perform a routine about the Prophet Muhammad to test his claims about free speech within the country.

C.K. quickly clarified that Chappelle is a Muslim, telling Maher, "So, it depends on who you are and what you want to talk about."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Talk show host Jimmy Kimmel also put comedian Aziz Ansari in the hot seat shortly after his performance at the festival.

"They murdered a journalist. These are not good people over there," Kimmel told Ansari, in reference to the infamous state-sponsored murder of Jamal Khashoggi inside the Saudi consulate in Turkey in 2018.

"I was just there to do a show for the people," Ansari replied. "Whenever there’s repressive societies like this, they try to keep things out — whether it’s rock ‘n’ roll music or blue jeans — because it makes people curious about outside ideas, outside values. And this is a very young country. Like, half the country is under the age of 25, and things can really change. And, to me, a comedy festival felt like something that’s pushing things to be more open and to push a dialogue."

Fox News Digital reached out to Yankovic and the General Entertainment Authority in Saudi Arabia.

Fox News Digital’s Marc Tomasco contributed to this report.

item.title: Jacksonville Jaguars set at 8.5 win total after surprising 13-4 season and Wild Card loss to Buffalo
item.description: Trevor Lawrence's passing yards prop looks appealing as the Jacksonville Jaguars face a tougher schedule with an 8.5 win total entering 2025.
item.content:encoded:
Sometimes these exercises in writing about teams can be a lot of fun because they remind me of the previous season and all that happened. It isn’t often that I remember everything about a situation, but I feel like I do a generally good job of keeping track of how the previous season went.

It becomes a blur to a certain extent, though. Try and name the last five Super Bowl losers, it is often harder than the winner. Honestly, I completely forgot about the Jacksonville Jaguars, but they were surprisingly good last season.

Jacksonville was able to steal the division last season and they were even 13-4 overall. The team was 10-2 against the AFC, and scored 138 more points than they allowed. They also ended the season hotter than almost any team in the game, winning their last eight games.

BETTING PREVIEW FOR PATRIOTS AFTER FALLING SHORT IN THE SUPER BOWL AND CONTROVERSIAL OFFSEASON

After Week 10, they were 5-4 and coming off of a loss to the Houston Texans. They closed out the season with wins over the Chargers, Cardinals, Titans (twice), Colts (twice), New York and Denver. Denver and Los Angeles were playoff teams, but the other six games were against fairly weak competition. They lost a heartbreaker to Buffalo in the Wild Card round, dropping that one 27-24.

There wasn’t a ton of stuff the Jaguars needed to do. They are a very good club and solid roster. They did lose Travis Etienne to the Saints, but most people will tell you that running backs are easily replaced. I’m not sure Etienne is that elite of a back that the Jaguars will have a big issue.

They signed a few key players on the line of scrimmage to extensions, but they did lose Devin Lloyd and Greg Newsome. Letting those guys walk did give them some picks so it might not be that big of a loss long term, even if it does hurt this season.

The team has quarterback Trevor Lawrence, who might be the most difficult quarterback for me to evaluate in the NFL. There is no question, he was awesome last year. He had the 6th most yards, was fifth in touchdowns, but did still throw 12 interceptions.

JOE BURROW CALLS BENGALS ROSTER THE 'MOST TALENTED' THE TEAM'S HAD, HAS LOFTY EXPECTATIONS FOR SEASON

He was also middle of the road as far as QBR. He has 98 touchdowns and 58 interceptions in his 77 games. There is another player who has 83 games, 89 touchdowns, and 55 interceptions – their yardage is about the same. That’s Daniel Jones, so you can make a decision on if you think Lawrence is great or not.

Either way he has had multiple coaches and schemes, so I don’t blame him completely. The rest of the offense is fine – Brian Thomas is a solid receiver, as is Jakobi Meyers, and anything you get from Travis Hunter is bonus. They have strong, young defense as well, punctuated by Hunter at cornerback. I’m interested to see how their linebackers play without Lloyd, but he wasn’t playing all three downs normally anyway.

The Jacksonville Jaguars are listed at 8.5 for their win total. That’s a major step back. If I look at their schedule, they have a bye week on Week 7 and I think they could very well be 1-5 if things don’t go well. 2-3 or 3-2 seems more likely, though. They have a tougher schedule this year, but should still win seven games without much issue. Getting another two from the list does seem like it could be a challenge. I think I’d stay away from the win total.

I do think Lawrence will go over 3,774.5 passing yards, though. He has gone over 4,000 in three of his five seasons. In 2024, when he played only 10 games, he had 2,045. He would’ve gone under that year too at the same pace. I think with Etienne leaving and his second year in the offensive system he should throw more. I don’t think he is great and I’m willing to bet the over if that gives you confidence.

item.title: Mamdani's latest Netanyahu remarks deepen concerns among Jewish leaders
item.description: Jewish leaders say NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani's admission he can't arrest Benjamin Netanyahu does little to ease concerns about his divisive rhetoric.
item.content:encoded:
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani's recent admission that he lacks the legal authority to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has done little to ease ongoing tensions between himself and the Jewish community. Jewish leaders told Fox News Digital that they are still concerned about the mayor's rhetoric, which they believe deepens divisions at a time of heightened concern over antisemitism.

Israel has remained one of the defining points of tension between Mamdani and the Jewish community in New York City since his campaign. When running for mayor, Mamdani said that he would seek to arrest Netanyahu, despite many pointing out that he did not have the authority to do so, which he ultimately admitted on Tuesday.

The issue resurfaced this week after Mamdani released a video explaining that while City Hall lacks the authority to arrest Netanyahu, he believes the prime minister should be held accountable under the International Criminal Court's warrant.

MAMDANI GOES BACK ON CAMPAIGN PROMISE, SAYS NYC CAN'T ARREST NETANYAHU

In a video posted on social media, Mamdani called Netanyahu "a war criminal" and "the architect of a horrific genocide against the Palestinian people."

"My administration has reviewed every avenue available under applicable law to determine whether New York City could execute the International Criminal Court's arrest warrant if Benjamin Netanyahu came here. It is clear that we do not have the independent legal authority to enforce this warrant," he said.

Nevertheless, he added that the Israeli leader was "not welcome in New York City."

Jewish leaders who spoke with Fox News Digital said the mayor's legal concession did little to address the community's concerns about Mamdani's rhetoric, which they believe fuels division.

Additionally, during a news conference Wednesday, Mamdani was asked how he believed New Yorkers should respond to Netanyahu's expected visit for the annual United Nations General Assembly in September.

"I think the bedrocks of our city is protest. It is something that has been a part of what makes our city so special, that New Yorkers can express themselves, whether they are in support or in opposition, no matter on whatever topic," he said.

MAMDANI DODGES ON ‘POLITICAL THEATER’ OF EMPTY NETANYAHU ARREST THREAT, CALLS FOR US ACTION AND NYC PROTESTS

Orthodox Union Executive Vice President and COO Rabbi Dr. Josh Joseph said the remarks were especially concerning given recent protests over the Israel-Hamas war.

"We know that the protests in the last few years have gotten violent at times," Joseph told Fox News Digital. "So, he's willing to risk inciting further violence based on misinformation."

Manhattan Jewish Experience (MJE) Founder and Director Rabbi Mark Wildes said that the mayor's remarks demonstrated a broader hostility toward Israel rather than criticism of a government official.

"What's upsetting to us in the Jewish community is that he's saying these things just to continue to drum home his message that the Jewish state, the state of Israel, has no right to exist," Wildes told Fox News Digital.

Wildes said that Mamdani's criticisms, in his view, have "nothing to do with Netanyahu's policies" and rather it was about "the Jewish people's right to defend themselves after being attacked, which is the only thing which is being done in Gaza and Lebanon."

The MJE leader added that the mayor's comments, particularly his sentiment that Netanyahu was "not welcome," risk further alienating Jewish New Yorkers at a time when they already feel vulnerable and disconnected from City Hall. He said the remark encapsulated how Jewish New Yorkers were feeling.

"For a leader in New York to say, 'You're not welcome here,' is upsetting, obviously, but it's consistent," Wildes said. "There's nothing he's saying that's inconsistent with the way he ran, with the kind of agenda that he has, he's been pro-Hamas, pro-terrorism since day one, and he's just showing his true colors."

Mamdani has been critical of Hamas — he condemned anti-Israel protesters chanting in support of the terrorist group earlier this year — but he has been criticized for being more strident in his rhetoric against Israel.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Joseph similarly warned that Mamdani needed to "remember that his words matter" as the leader of New York City.

Despite their criticism of the mayor, both Wildes and Joseph remain confident in the resilience of New York's Jewish community. Wildes argued that the heightened political tensions would not deter the Jewish community's connection to Israel or New York City.

"Am Yisrael Chai is not just a slogan. Am Yisrael Chai means the Jewish people are alive. Israel is thriving, and Israel is continuing to grow," Wildes said.

Mamdani's office did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment.

item.title: Sophie Cunningham and West Wilson split on transgender athletes in girls' sports despite podcast partnership
item.description: West Wilson called the transgender athletes debate a "borderline nonexistent issue" pushed by right-wingers, putting him at odds with Sophie Cunningham.
item.content:encoded:
WNBA star Sophie Cunningham ruffled plenty of feathers with her recent comments regarding protecting women's sports.

Several media personalities and even some fellow WNBA colleagues were quick to bristle at her statement about keeping biological men out of girls' sports, but the Indiana Fever guard has not backed down.

The latest person to take umbrage with Cunningham's comments is a familiar and unlikely one, though, as childhood friend and podcast co-host, West Wilson, took to X to voice his displeasure with "right wingers" turning the trans in women's sports debate into a mountain of an issue.

WHITE HOUSE DEFENDS WNBA STAR SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM AFTER SHE SPEAKS OUT IN SUPPORT OF PROTECTING WOMEN'S SPORTS

"Transgender athletes in American sports is such a borderline nonexistent issue that right-wingers have convinced a massive portion of people in our country that these people are a threat to sports in America when mathematically, that's not the case at all," Wilson said.

He continued by claiming that by platforming the issue, politicians in particular are sowing divisiveness and "isolating" trans people.

"There is, like, 10 transgender athletes in all of the NCAA," Wilson said. "I think there are unique questions that can be handled on individual bases, but to allow this to take our attention from housing, healthcare, wars, all the other actual harmful s–t in our country is dumb."

MEGAN RAPINOE SAYS EFFORTS TO BAR TRANS ATHLETES FROM WOMEN'S SPORTS ARE 'ATTACK ON WOMEN IN SOCIETY'

There are plenty of things wrong with what Wilson said, namely that transgender athletes in female sports is solely a "right wing" issue.

Plenty of sane people on both sides of the aisle have voiced their displeasure with biological men invading female spaces, so to paint this as a fringe right crusade is disingenuous.

It's also worth noting that he goes out of his way to mention NCAA athletes but nothing about youth or high school sports.

MICHIGAN FATHER ALLEGES BOMB THREAT TO HOME AFTER DAUGHTER SPOKE UP ABOUT FACING TRANS ATHLETE WITHOUT KNOWING

While the issue of transgender athletes in college sports is still an issue worth fighting, many people are far more concerned with this happening at the youth and high school level, something that OutKick has covered extensively in the past.

Finally, it seems we've gone from "this isn't happening" to "it's only happening a little," representing a classic slide down the proverbial slippery slope.

What's perhaps even more interesting in all of this is how Cunningham and Wilson will work around this difference of opinion.

SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST SPORTS NEWS

Cunningham has made her stance pretty clear and even doubled down on it, while Wilson appears to be completely on the other side.

While some political differences like tax rates can be amicably disagreed on, the transgender issue continues to be a hot-button one.

It remains to be seen how the two will handle their differences, but suffice to say it doesn't sound like either will be budging anytime soon.

item.title: Riley Gaines calls USA Today reporter 'insane' for invoking Emmett Till in column about Caitlin Clark
item.description: Riley Gaines, the host of “The Riley Gaines Show," torched USA Today writer Nancy Armour over her recent Caitlin Clark column, calling her "insane."
item.content:encoded:
Riley Gaines, the host of "The Riley Gaines Show," torched USA Today writer Nancy Armour over her recent and controversial Caitlin Clark column.

In the opinion piece published earlier this week, Armour compared the lynching of Emmett Till to Caitlin Clark putting "Black" and "queer" WNBA players "in danger."

"It shouldn’t need reminding this country has an awful history of Black people being harmed, even killed, in the name of 'defending' White women. The irony of the WNBA's All-Star Game is that it's happening this weekend in Chicago, the hometown of Emmett Till, who became an icon of the civil rights movement after his tragic murder," Amour wrote.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"The local art gallery is currently hosting an exhibit imagining his life if he hadn't been lynched. While it’s incumbent on the WNBA to do more to protect its players, there also should be an expectation on Clark to recognize the broader implications of her actions being weaponized. "

Of all the bad takes about Clark, Gaines said Armour’s was the "worst one by a mile," adding that she was dumbfounded by the comparison.

"Do you realize what Nancy Armour is doing there? She's connecting Emmett Till's lynching to Caitlin Clark's talent and skill set and behavior on the basketball court. Excuse me?" Gaines said on a recent episode of "The Riley Gaines Show."

Gaines continued her excoriation of Armour, calling the writer "insane" for comparing Till’s lynching to Clark’s actions on the basketball court. Till was a 14-year-old Black teen who was abducted, tortured and eventually lynched in 1955 Mississippi after an accusation from a White woman

USA TODAY REPORTER APOLOGIZES FOR INVOKING EMMETT TILL IN COLUMN ABOUT CAITLIN CLARK AFTER UPSETTING THE WOKE

"These people are insane," Gaines said. "They have lost their ability to think rationally. That is literally dead and gone. In what world do those two things connect? Honestly, even after reading the piece I don't know where she's going with this."

Gaines proceeded to call Armour an all-time "rage-baiter."

"Maybe it's just like all-time rage bait. Like dropping Emmett Till's name in an article about the WNBA All-Star game, that's got to be an all-time rage baiter. I don't know, maybe I'm falling for it. Maybe this is what Nancy Armor wanted," Gaines said.

Armour apologized for invoking Till in her column and called it an "inartful comparison."

"In my recent column, I made an inartful comparison with the murder of Emmett Till. I intended to connect the issues the WNBA is currently facing with its All-Star Game being hosted in Till’s hometown of Chicago," Armour wrote in an apology posted Thursday on Bluesky.

"I obviously did not provide enough context for that."

item.title: Transgender dolls to be available for Minnesota schoolchildren as young as 4 under Walz-backed program: report
item.description: Taxpayer-funded transgender dolls with swappable genitalia target children ages 4-10 through a University of Minnesota research program tied to Tim Walz.
item.content:encoded:
Transgender dolls will be accessible to Minnesota school children between the ages of four and 10 starting this fall as a result of a taxpayer-funded development program supported by Gov. Tim Walz, according to a report.

The MyGenderDolls, which were developed in part through the University of Minnesota’s Early Innovation Fund, will be for use by "clinicians and educators" starting this year, the New York Post first reported, citing the product's website.

The dolls, according to the website, were "designed for gender diverse children ages 4–10."

SEN HAWLEY WARNS IT WOULD BE 'UNCONSCIONABLE' IF BILLIONS OF TAXPAYER FUNDS FLOW TO TRANS KIDS’ SEX CHANGES

They come with interchangeable accessories and removable and swappable genitalia to help children "realize all the different options that exist for who they can be — regardless of their body parts," University of Minnesota postdoctoral fellow Ben Parchem, Ph.D., said in a now-deleted article in the University of Minnesota Foundation's magazine.

The dolls began as a research program in the University of Minnesota Medical School's Department of Family Medicine and Community Health, spearheaded by two members of the school's faculty, Dianne Berg, PhD, and G. Nic Rider, PhD, both educators in the school's Department of Family Medicine and Community Health.

"It’s really important to address the belief, ‘I’m not a 'real' boy because I don’t have these private parts,’ versus, ‘I am a real boy, whatever my anatomy looks like,’" Berg told the Foundation's magazine in the now-deleted article.

"It’s about helping children develop tools to cope with messages in society that could lead to shame," she added.

VIRGINIA SCHOOL DISTRICT SUED OVER ALLEGED POLICY OF KEEPING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS HIDDEN FROM PARENTS

"MyGender Dolls began as an idea of the Institute for Sexual and Gender Health psychologist, Rachel Becker-Warner, PsyD. NCGSH Co-Director, Dianne Berg, PhD, and Communications Specialist, Ashley Finch, have been hard at work developing the dolls to be used as a therapeutic tool for transgender and gender diverse children. The concept is similar to classic paper dolls; kids can select bodies, genitals, clothes, and other accessories as a way to visualize their anatomy and genders," a now deleted 2024 summary of the project from the University of Minnesota's Eli Coleman Institute for Sexual and Gender Health read. 

The project is one of many pro-transgender state-funded efforts under Walz, according to the Post.

In 2023, the University of Minnesota’s Eli Coleman Institute for Sexual and Gender Health (ISGH) presented Walz with the Distinguished Sexual and Gender Health Champion Award "for his outstanding efforts in protecting sexual and reproductive health care (PRO Act, HF 1) and gender-affirming health care (Executive Order 23-03) in Minnesota," the school wrote in its annual report in 2023.

WALZ POST CALLING SCOTUS GIRLS' SPORTS RULING 'CRUEL' BACKFIRES ONLINE AS CRITICS REVEAL WHAT'S EVEN CRUELER

Of the three faculty members presenting him his award, one was Rider, a co-creator of MyGenderDolls.

Fox News Digital contacted Walz's office, MyGenderDolls, Rider, the University of Minnesota and the school's Department of Family Medicine and Community Health for added comment.

item.title: Three SEC win totals you should absolutely pounce on before the 2026 college football season begins
item.description: Arch Manning's Texas Longhorns, Mike Elko's Texas A&M Aggies, and Lane Kiffin's LSU Tigers headline three SEC win totals worth watching in 2026.
item.content:encoded:
With the conclusion of SEC Media Days, we now officially begin the mad dash toward the opening of the college football season.

It might seem like this offseason has moved at a snail's pace, but speaking from experience, things really start to pick up after Media Days and before you know it, you're knee-deep in the regular season.

Before we reach that point, though, we have some predictions to make, and there's no better to start than to look at some of my favorite SEC win totals heading into the 2026 season.

PERCEPTION IS REALITY, AND THE SEC NEEDS TO START WINNING AGAIN BEFORE IT CONTINUES TO PUFF OUT ITS CHEST

Here are three juicy win totals for a trio of SEC squads that I absolutely love as we hurtle towards the start of my favorite time of the year.

If there was ever going to be a year that Texas and head coach Steve Sarkisian put it all together, it would be 2026.

That alone should be enough to hammer the over on this one, since nine wins almost certainly would leave the Longhorns' College Football Playoff hopes in limbo, but there's more to it than that.

This is one of the most talented rosters in the country, cultivated through multiple top-five recruiting classes over the past few cycles and supplemented by the third-ranked portal class heading into the season.

The pieces are there, but what puts Texas over the top is having another year of Arch Manning.

The redshirt junior signal caller sputtered to start the first half of 2025, but by November, Manning was one of the best quarterbacks in the country and should carry that over into this year.

The Horns play a pretty tough schedule in 2026, but a week two showdown against Ohio State should tell us a lot.

If Texas handles the Buckeyes at home, the over will almost assuredly hit.

FIVE SEC TRAP GAMES IN 2026 THAT COULD UPEND THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RACE, FROM LSU TO GEORGIA

Staying in the Lone Star State, let's travel due east to College Station.

If this were two or three years ago, I would have fallen all over myself to smash the under, considering it was almost a meme for the Aggies to finish 8-4 following any given season.

That seems to have changed since head coach Mike Elko got to town.

In just his second year, Elko was able to guide the Aggies to an 11-win season and a Playoff berth. Now he was the luxury of a veteran signal caller returning in Marcel Reed, along with two stellar wide receivers in Mario Craver and incoming transfer Isaiah Horton.

Texas A&M also ranks top-20 nationally in returning production on defense, and I trust any Elko coached team to look really solid on that side of the ball.

The Aggies will be tested a bunch on the road this season, particularly in games against Oklahoma and Alabama, but I trust the steady hand of third-year starter Reed and a veteran team to be the deciding factor.

Nine wins feels more than doable here. Take over.

If you've been paying attention to anything I've written in the past six months, you know how high I am on the LSU Tigers this coming season and beyond.

For starters, they went out and hired Lane Kiffin as their head coach, who was fresh a historic run of leading the Ole Miss Rebels to their first ever College Football Playoff appearance.

Kiffin's staff is also noteworthy, retaining Tigers' defensive coordinator Blake Baker and bringing Charlie Weis Jr. over from Oxford as his OC.

In addition to a dynamite coaching staff, LSU brought in the number one transfer portal class, featuring the top-ranked quarterback (Sam Leavitt), offensive tackle (Jordan Seaton), and edge rusher (Princewill Umanmielen).

The hope in Baton Rouge is that the marriage of elite (and expensive) talent and a stellar coaching staff will bear fruit in year one, so anything less than a CFP appearance will be seen as a colossal failure, both locally and nationally.

Eight wins certainly won't be accepted by any of the Tiger faithful, so it almost feels like a given that the baseline for Kiffin and co. is set at 9-3.

With the September matchups against Clemson and Ole Miss, we should know very early on what this team is made of.

If the Tigers start 4-0 in the first month of the season, I'll be feeling pretty good about the win total, though they certainly won't be out of the woods by any stretch. But 2–2 or worse, and it might be time to cash out before the calendar flips to October.

item.title: Biden judge blocking Ethiopian deportations despite SCOTUS ruling clashed with ICE before
item.description: Back-to-back rulings in Massachusetts blocked TPS terminations for Ethiopia and South Sudan, sparking fierce debate over lower court authority.
item.content:encoded:
A Biden-appointed federal judge on Friday became the second jurist in Massachusetts to block the Trump administration's effort to end Temporary Protected Status for migrant groups, fueling a growing clash over whether lower courts are ignoring a recent Supreme Court ruling that narrowed their authority over such decisions.

U.S. District Judge Brian Murphy of the District of Massachusetts issued an administrative stay in African Communities Together v. Mullin, temporarily preserving TPS protections for Ethiopian nationals while the court considers whether plaintiffs may pursue constitutional claims in light of the Supreme Court's June ruling. In a 6-3 decision in Mullin v. Doe, the Supreme Court significantly narrowed lower courts' authority to block DHS decisions designating or terminating TPS.

Murphy's ruling drew a swift response from DHS General Counsel James Percival, who accused him of "mutiny" against the Supreme Court and revived criticism of the judge's May 2025 order halting a deportation flight to South Sudan. DHS blamed Murphy for leaving ICE officers stranded at a U.S. military base in Djibouti, where officials said they faced malaria exposure and the threat of rocket attacks from terrorist groups in neighboring Yemen.

SUPREME COURT'S LATEST IMMIGRATION RULING WILL CAUSE AMERICANS TO 'DIE AND SUFFER' ATTORNEY WARNS

"Remember when that district judge rerouted a plane with child rapists headed for South Sudan? The judge made ICE land in Djibouti to face Malaria and terrorist rocket attacks from Yemen," Percival wrote on X. "Fun fact: it was the very same Judge Brian Murphy who entered a lawless TPS order today!"

Murphy's Friday order comes amid a months-long legal fight over the Trump administration's effort to end Ethiopia's TPS designation.

The litigation began after then-Department of Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem determined in December 2025 that conditions in Ethiopia no longer justified Temporary Protected Status and announced the designation would terminate. Under the department's notice, Ethiopia's TPS designation was set to expire after a 60-day wind-down period, with protections ending on Feb. 13, 2026, before Judge Brian Murphy intervened.

SUPREME COURT WEIGHS TRUMP EFFORT TO TERMINATE TEMPORARY PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIAN, SYRIAN MIGRANTS

Earlier this year, Murphy sided with the challengers, granting their motion to postpone DHS's termination of Ethiopia's TPS designation after finding they were likely to succeed on claims that the department failed to follow the procedures Congress established for ending TPS.

But litigation was upended on June 25 after the Supreme Court ruled in Mullin v. Doe that lower courts generally cannot hear Administrative Procedure Act challenges to DHS decisions designating or terminating TPS. Since the Administrative Procedure Act formed the legal backbone of the plaintiffs' challenge, the Trump administration argued Murphy's injunction had been undermined and should be lifted.

However, the Supreme Court left open whether constitutional claims could still proceed, leading the plaintiffs to revise their complaint to focus on those arguments.

BLUE STATE LEADERS ERUPT AFTER SUPREME COURT’S DECISION ENDING TPS PROTECTIONS FOR HAITIANS, SYRIANS

Murphy's ruling comes just hours after another judge in the District of Massachusetts, Senior U.S. District Judge Patti Saris, temporarily halted the Trump administration's effort to terminate TPS for South Sudan. Saris issued an administrative stay preserving protections while she considers whether plaintiffs may amend their lawsuit following the Supreme Court's ruling. Like the Ethiopia case, the South Sudan challenge was brought by African Communities Together along with individual TPS holders.

Saris said her order was simply meant to temporarily maintain the status quo while the court considers the case and was "not a ruling on the merits."

The tandem rulings have led to calls for the Trump administration to ignore the lower courts' ruling.

"These Democrat operatives in robes do not have the power to do this," Mike Davis, a conservative legal activist and founder of the Article III Project, wrote on X. "The Supreme Court just made that crystal clear. So it's time to ignore these clearly lawless orders."

"These puny little district court judges have been overruled so many times by the supreme court, especially on immigration, I think it's time for the president to take his constitutional oath seriously, and ignore them," Ann Coulter, a conservative political commentator wrote on X.

Murphy has repeatedly clashed with the Supreme Court over the Trump administration's immigration policies, with the justices twice siding with the administration in its challenge to his orders restricting deportations of illegal aliens to countries that are not their homelands.

The Biden administration first granted Ethiopians Temporary Protected Status in 2022, declaring that war and a worsening humanitarian crisis had made it unsafe to return them to their home country. Then-DHS Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas pointed to ongoing armed conflict, widespread violence, human rights abuses, food insecurity, among the many reason as the basis for the designation. The protections took effect on Dec. 12, 2022, and were later extended through Dec. 12, 2025. DHS estimated approximately 26,700 Ethiopian nationals living in the United States could qualify for TPS.

Fox News Digital reached out to African Communities Together for comment.

item.title: WNBA All-Star Game betting preview: Team Coop's guards could give them the edge over Team Spoon
item.description: The WNBA All-Star Game features Caitlin Clark and A'ja Wilson on Team Spoon against Paige Bueckers and Breanna Stewart on Team Coop tonight.
item.content:encoded:
You probably didn't know it, but the WNBA has been off for a few days now because of the All-Star Game that takes place tonight. I know that you missed it, but now we have some women's basketball back, so don't be too upset! Jokes aside, I've enjoyed this season despite the same narratives being pushed.

Betting on the sport has proved very profitable and rewarding to this point as well. This is an exhibition, but I do think we have an edge here.

MARINA MABREY TIES WNBA SINGLE-GAME SCORING RECORD WITH 53 POINTS IN TEMPO'S HISTORIC WIN

The teams are basically divided by fan voting, player, and coaches. I don't think it is really important to get into how the players got here, but you should know who is on what team. For Team Coop, they have Paige Bueckers as their main attraction. If you're not familiar with Bueckers' game, you should be. She is elite in many ways. A great scorer, a solid playmaker, and even good on defense.

What I like most about this team is that they have a lot of talented guards. If they want to get out and run, they shouldn't have any trouble.

Kahleah Copper is one of the most elite finishers in the game. Marina Mabrey is a lethal outside shooter. Sonia Citron is one of the better young players and a talented scorer. Kelsey Mitchell is one of my favorite players in the league and a versatile scorer. That doesn't mention Breanna Stewart, who is still one of the best players in the league, and Angel Reese, who will play with energy and effort no matter if this is an exhibition or if it actually meant something. Their team is very good.

You're certainly familiar with their Captain, Caitlin Clark. Clark was going to be an All-Star based on popularity, but her performance on the court shows she deserves to be here. Expect that she doesn't do quite a bit in this game, though. She is likely going to pass and facilitate much more than look to score.

I could see her shooting from deep, but I don't think that she is going to just jack up shots like they do in the men's version of this game.

CAITLIN CLARK MAKES WNBA HISTORY WITH RECORD-BREAKING GAME AFTER WEEKS OF CONTROVERSY

The rest of the team is rounded out mostly by forwards/centers — Aliyah Boston is really good and familiar with Clark, being that they are on the same team. A'ja Wilson is the best player in the WNBA, but I don't think she is going to try all that hard in this game.

Jonquel Jones, Nneka Ogwumike, and Kiki Iriafen will round out that group. They should be able to get a bucket just about whenever they want, but they are better closer to the basket than farther away. Oliva Miles is one person who stands out to me as someone who might pour in buckets for Team Spoon.

The scores from the past few years are interesting. Last year, the total went to 282. The year prior, it was just 226. In 2023, they were at 270, and in 2022 they scored just 246. Tonight's total is 277.5. I think that is too high. The women can score, don't get me wrong, but I think the chances of them just pouring in points is more likely for Team Coop than for Team Spoon. The game is also in the United Center, which is notorious for being tougher to shoot in for many players.

Not only will I back the under, but I'll also take Team Cooper. If either team is likely to run the floor and play in a game with little defense, I think the guards will be more energetic and ready to go. They are getting +3.5 points, and I think some of that is because Clark is on the team, and some maybe because of Wilson. I'll still take the points with Cooper.

item.title: Fired school counselor loses again after free speech fight over gender-themed books in his office
item.description: The 9th Circuit ruled an Oregon school counselor's book display promoting binary gender views was government speech, not protected by the First Amendment.
item.content:encoded:
A federal appeals court ruled earlier this week that a now-fired Oregon school counselor’s display of books promoting binary gender views to students was not protected by the First Amendment.

The 2-1 decision handed down by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Tuesday upheld Roderick E. Theis II’s termination from Oregon’s InterMountain Education Service District (IMESD), according to court documents obtained by Fox News Digital.

The court also rejected Theis’ appeal.

CHICAGO COLLEGE REMOVES LGBTQ PRIDE FLAG OVER INSTITUTIONAL NEUTRALITY CONCERNS

According to the ruling, Theis, an education specialist who worked for the IMESD for more than 15 years, displayed books titled "He is He" and "She is She" in two separate offices on different campuses when meeting with middle school students.

He also displayed a children’s book penned by conservative commentator Matt Walsh titled "Johnny the Walrus" that "allegorically comments on transgender issues," court documents said.

Following an investigation into the incident, Theis told school administrators that he did not mean any harm by displaying the books and even considered putting them away when transgender-identifying students visited his office.

WISCONSIN TEACHER FIRED AFTER SOCIAL MEDIA POST ADVOCATING TO 'MAKE AMERICANS GREAT ASSASSINS AGAIN'

However, IMESD concluded the display of the books was a "bias incident" and instructed the counselor to remove them from his school offices — or risk termination.

A federal judge later partially granted Theis’ request for a protective order that allowed him to continue displaying the books in his offices when students were not visiting, but his employment was ultimately terminated after a district investigation revealed Theis provided the books to middle school students who had requested to see them, according to the ruling.

Theis’ attorneys went on to argue that the counselor was protected from the injunction when meeting with students outside their official sessions, but a lower court later ruled that the partial injunction prohibited Theis from displaying the books when students were present in his office.

GOP LAWMAKERS URGE SUPREME COURT TO STRENGTHEN FIRST AMENDMENT PROTECTIONS FOR STREET PREACHERS

The lower court, however, issued another ruling against Theis’ termination appeal.

The ruling was upheld by the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Tuesday, with the majority opinion outlining longstanding precedents that an educators’ speech is considered government speech when interacting with students.

"As a government employee, Theis was assigned to work in school offices, meet with students, and carry out his duties in that setting," Circuit Judge John B. Owens wrote in the majority ruling. "His speech occurred in the course of those responsibilities and cannot be meaningfully separated from them. As such, Theis’s speech falls outside the First Amendment’s ambit."

In a statement to Fox News Digital, Mathew Hoffman, legal counsel at Alliance Defending Freedom, vowed that Theis' attorneys are "evaluating next steps" following the ruling. 

"The government can’t silence a speaker just because it disapproves of what he says, yet InterMountain fired Rod Theis after a single person objected to his views," Hoffman added. "We will continue to defend Rod’s First Amendment freedom to express his views like other employees."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The sole dissenting opinion, written by Circuit Judge Lawrence VanDyke, sharply criticized the ruling. VanDyke argued that Theis’ books should be considered personal decorative items in his office, while questioning if a school could permit employees to hang pro-Palestinian banners while simultaneously banning the display of the Israeli flag.

"Could public school administrators establish a policy allowing office decoration with partisan political messages deemed sufficiently ‘compassionate,’ but prohibit — as inherently hostile — any political speech that did not align with the Democratic Socialists of America platform?" VanDyke wrote.

Fox News Digital reached out to IMESD for comment.

item.title: The biggest food and drink mistakes travelers make on flights, experts warn
item.description: Experts reveal the common nutrition mistakes travelers make that worsen bloating, dehydration and fatigue — and the electrolyte-rich foods to pack instead.
item.content:encoded:
Flying can take a toll on the body in many ways, but experts say there are simple nutrition rules travelers should follow to reduce common problems like bloating, dehydration, dry skin and fatigue.

Air travel exposes travelers to changes in cabin humidity, pressure and oxygen levels that can affect overall comfort, with the dry cabin air being the biggest contributor to dehydration.

In addition to thirst, dehydration can cause headaches, low energy, muscle cramps and dizziness. In more severe cases, it can also lead to confusion and fainting.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Travelers are prone to making several mistakes that contribute to dehydration, experts say. Many people avoid consuming liquids when they travel to cut down on bathroom breaks.

Some are also likely to opt for foods that are salty, greasy and heavy. It's also common to load up on caffeine and alcohol, which can contribute to bloating, constipation, dehydration and electrolyte imbalance.

Health experts advise hydrating before, during and after a flight. Bring your own water bottle that you can sip slowly and refill, so you don’t have to rely on onboard beverages.

"By the time you feel thirsty, your body is already dehydrated," Lindsay Baker, a director at the Gatorade Sports Science Institute, told Eating Well. "It is better to plan ahead and make sure you are well-hydrated before you start your trip. This helps avoid the need to drink large volumes of fluid to ‘catch up’ on hydration later."

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

Drinking water alone may not be enough, according to Baker.

"Your body needs electrolytes to hold onto the water you’re drinking," she said.

Electrolytes are naturally found in foods like bananas, spinach and avocados and are also available in drink mixes and tablets.

Carbonated drinks, such as soda, sparkling water and beer, also make bloating worse by adding gas to the stomach. 

Alcohol, and excessive caffeine intake, may contribute to dehydration and are best avoided when flying, experts say.

"If you do want to drink alcohol, opt for something like a single Bloody Mary — tomato juice is a source of electrolytes as well as being antioxidant rich," Stephanie Smith, a women’s health nutritionist for Agora Health, told CNT Travler.

The reduced cabin pressure on airplanes can cause gas in the digestive tract to expand, leading to bloating. To minimize this effect, experts advise avoiding gas-producing foods, such as beans, lentils, broccoli, cabbage, onions and Brussels sprouts. 

Eat smaller, lighter meals, since large, heavy meals slow digestion and leave more food sitting in the stomach.

Overly sweet and salty foods should also be avoided. High-sodium foods can increase thirst and may contribute to temporary bloating during flights.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

"I suggest people avoid snacks high in simple carbohydrates or added sugars without other macronutrients to properly balance them out," Marra Burroughs, a doctor of clinical nutrition and registered dietitian, told Travel + Leisure.

"Traveling is exhausting to begin with, and a poorly balanced carb-heavy snack can lead to a crash that can worsen the experience and add to fatigue," Burroughs added. "If you want to partake in a snack that is higher in sugar, I recommend pairing it with fat and protein to balance it out."

It’s best to steer clear of ultra-processed snacks at the airport and choose protein-forward options such as unsalted nuts, Greek yogurt, cheese sticks and hard-boiled eggs.

Nutrient-dense water-rich foods such as watermelon, grapes, cucumbers and celery can also help travelers stay hydrated.

Flying on an empty stomach is also a bad idea, experts say, because low blood sugar can contribute to fatigue, irritability and dizziness during travel. Eating a well-balanced meal a couple of hours before a flight is advised.

item.title: Tony Romo's brutal golf score before getting arrested paints a nightmarish picture
item.description: Tony Romo was arrested for operating while intoxicated in Milwaukee after finishing 35-over par at the Wisconsin Amateur Championship golf tournament.
item.content:encoded:
I don't know Jim!

Yes, Tony Romo is making headlines, again, for all the wrong reasons ahead of this 2026 NFL season.

For those who missed it, the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback was arrested in Milwaukee Thursday night for allegedly operating while intoxicated.

TONY ROMO ARRESTED IN MILWAUKEE FOR ALLEGED OWI OFFENSE: REPORT

Romo was reportedly stopped on a highway and performed poorly on field sobriety tests, FOX6 in Milwaukee reported. He was released and is due in court Sept. 21.

I'm not here to break down the Xs and Os of Romo's arrest, and what it might mean for his future at CBS. I don't care about that. I care about what Romo was doing before his ill-fated drive home.

FORMER COWBOYS QB TONY ROMO FALLS SHORT IN US OPEN GOLF QUALIFYING BID

The 46-year-old was arrested on the same day as the final round of the Wisconsin Amateur Championship golf tournament. Romo is an excellent golfer, and was playing in the event. Last week, he played in the American Century Championship celebrity golf tournament.

His offseasons are mostly spent on a golf course, which is fair. It's where I'd be, too.

Here's the thing ... this particular event didn't go great for Romo. Boots on the ground reported that he finished the tournament a whopping 35-over par and won just $60.

Thirty-five over par!

My God. What a card!

Look, I'm not gonna rag on Romo for a bad few days of golf. He's an elite golfer — for an amateur — and I am awful. I usually sit around 85, and that's only if my short game cooperates.

It usually doesn't.

That being said, it's still wild to see a +35 on the scorecard. Lordy.

Now, the course was obviously a hornets nest. I know this because a quick Google search tells me the winner finished at +3. The cut-line was +15. Sounds like a nightmare. Frankly, it sounds like I'd blow through a dozen Noodles before the turn. Maybe more.

But man, seeing Tony Romo card a +35 and then get pulled over for operating while under the influence is a doozy. I'm not sitting here condoning drinking and then driving, obviously. That's a big no-no. It should never happen in this day in age. There are Ubers on every corner, even in West Bend, Wisconsin.

After shooting a 12-over in the final round, though? Tough look.

We've all been there.

item.title: 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan suffers significant injuries in offseason car wreck
item.description: San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shananhan was involved in a car accident last week, suffering non-life threatening injuries, the team announced on Saturday.
item.content:encoded:
San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shananhan was involved in a serious car wreck last week, the team announced on Saturday.

Shanahan broke his nose, three ribs, his hand, needed over 40 stitches in his face and suffered a severe concussion in the accident, according to ESPN. The incident happened on July 14 when the 45-year-old coach collided with another SUV by his home in northern California, according to the report.

"San Francisco 49ers Head Coach Kyle Shanahan was involved in a car accident last week where he suffered non-life-threatening injuries. Coach Shanahan will participate in team activities on a limited basis at the start of training camp while he recovers. Coach Shanahan and the 49ers organization would like to sincerely thank all first responders involved for their efforts and care," the 49ers said in a statement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

"Assistant Head Coach Chris Foerster along with team coordinators will handle head coach responsibilities during this period."

Palo Alto lieutenant Nicholas Martinez told ESPN that the other driver was not injured and that drugs or alcohol were not involved. Shanahan was taken to the hospital by local paramedics after the wreck and was released after spending much of the day there. 

"Consistent with our standard release of information procedures in such cases, we do not release information regarding the cause of the collision, or which party may have been at fault," Martinez told ESPN.

He told the outlet that no one was cited for the collision. 

The 49ers' training camp starts on Sunday, but Shanahan will not be allowed to participate until he is cleared by doctors. The longtime coach told his assistant coaches about the accident on Tuesday, according to the report.

49ers general manager John Lynch spoke on Saturday and said that while there aren't concussions protocols for staff, he will "basically" be in the same concussion protocol players go through. Lynch said the doctors will dictate when he comes back. 

"No. 1 for Kyle and the Shanahan family is getting him back right. He's a tremendous head coach , but this is bigger than that, this is about his well-being, and uh, we're going to take the time necessary and I think we're very equipped to do that," Lynch told reporters at a press conference.

Lynch said that Shanahan has been in the building, but he will not be running the team. The general manager did say that Shanahan will probably still be on the practice field despite the injuries, he just won't be running the show.  

Lynch didn't definitively saw Shanahan will be coaching in Week 1, but said that the expectation is he will be back long before the regular season begins. 

Shanahan is entering his 10th season as the 49ers head coach and is widely considered one of the best coaches in the NFL. Over nine seasons, he has an 82-67 record and has led the team to the Super Bowl twice. 

Shanahan is believed to be recovering well and healing at home, according to the report. The 49ers' first game of the season is against the Los Angeles Rams on Sept. 10 in Melbourne, Australia.
